text:
claudia: Security advisory: required migration away from long-lived OAuth client secrets used by internal apps. We've detected multiple occurrences of static app client secrets stored in repo-side config and some exposed by a browser extension report. This increases risk of token replay and automated scraping. Action: rotate and adopt short-lived client credentials (OAuth PKCE or client assertion flow) within 7 days.

rahul: Can you share the evidence? Which apps are affected?

claudia: Triage found 9 internal apps with static client secrets in repo snapshots and 3 cases where a reported extension exfiltrated a secret from a dev workstation. No signs of active misuse, but treat as compromised. We created SEC-3512 with the full list. Owners were DM'd.

dev-tools: Recommended migration pattern: 1) switch to PKCE for public clients, 2) use signed JWT client assertions (private key rotation) for service-to-service, 3) store short-lived tokens in the secrets manager and fetch at runtime. Docs: https://redwood.internal/docs/auth/short-lived-oauth.

maya: For services that can't support PKCE immediately (old runtime), what's the interim?

infra-oncall: Interim allowed-for-72h: issue a new client secret, rotate the old one, restrict the secret to specific IPs/egress rules and add a vault policy requiring auto-rotation. We're also enabling token-binding checks on the gateway for these clients.

claudia: Owner actions (mandatory): 1) Rotate any exposed client secret and replace usage with a short-lived flow or client-assertion before 2026-04-01T23:59:00Z. 2) Update SEC-3512 with rotation proof (secret-manager version or commit tag). 3) Remove secrets from repos and add git-secret-scan exceptions if necessary. Noncompliance will trigger automated key revocation.

sec-bot: SEC-3512 created and owners notified. Org-wide repo scan scheduled in 24h. Auto-revocation window set to 7 days for affected managed credentials.

rahul: I'm owner for internal-dashboard. Will opt into client-assertion and update SEC-3512 today.

claudia: Thanks. If you need help migrating, open a stub ticket labelled "oauth-migration" or ping @dev-tools for pairing. Reply with "ack" once you've updated the ticket.
